sections.html:
Three counters matter to a seller in Edmonson County, and all sit in Brownsville. Valuation belongs to the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), whose office is inside the courthouse on Main Cross Street at 270-597-2381. Payment belongs to the sheriff at 110 Jackson Street, 270-597-2157. Anything late, plus the land records, goes through the county clerk at 108 North Main Street, 270-597-2624.

County government keeps weekday hours starting at 7:30 and ending at 4:00. The PVA's website links a qPublic parcel search, which shows how a particular house is assessed before anyone picks up the phone.

No single office decides the total bill. The PVA supplies the value, while the levy comes from the taxing bodies, among them the fiscal court and the county school system. For the combined rate on one parcel, ask the sheriff.

Bills leave the sheriff's office on October 30, later than the statewide default of September, so the whole calendar here runs a month behind the usual one. If you have no bill by November 15, ring the sheriff, who mails a duplicate right away. The slower start fits the alternative schedule in KRS 134.015, which gives each stage one month when bills are delayed.

What the Edmonson County Sheriff charges at each stage of the collection year
When you payWhat you owe
Paid by November 30Bill less 2%
All of DecemberBill as printed
All of JanuaryBill plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Bill plus 21%

That 21 percent is a 10 percent penalty with a 10 percent sheriff fee stacked on it. Whatever remains unpaid when April 15 ends goes to the clerk.

The sheriff takes cash at the counter, plus checks, money orders and cards (processing fees apply to cards, by phone or in the office). The office opens at 7:30 every day it is open, closes at 4:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, and closes at noon on Thursday and Saturday.

sections.h2: How an Edmonson County owner contests a valuation
sections.html:
Talk to the PVA first, and appeal second. Values are struck on January 1. Houses can be listed with the PVA through March 1, and business equipment through May 15.

  • The assessment roll lies open for thirteen days starting on the first May Monday, including Saturdays.
  • A conference with the PVA or a deputy unlocks the right to appeal. The appeal form then goes to the clerk's office, due the workday after the inspection window shuts.
  • The local board sits for no more than five days, opening between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends.
  • Evidence decides the outcome: insurance policies, building costs, listings and physical details of the land. An appeal with none is denied.
  • Skipping a scheduled hearing forfeits any further review.

If bills print while an appeal is pending, they use the owner's stated figure, and a supplemental bill covers any increase the board later sets.

The state deducts $49,100 from a qualifying home's value, and that figure applies to the 2025 and 2026 rolls. Owners qualify at 65 or when classified as totally disabled, and the PVA takes the application.

For proof of age, a birth certificate, license or passport will do. A disability claim rests on classification under a federal program or a retirement system, with payments received over the whole year. Disability claims are renewed every year, unless the owner has a service-connected disability or has been ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: Selling an Edmonson County house while taxes are unpaid
sections.html:
The debt rides with the land. The lien outlives a change of owner: KRS 134.420 keeps it alive for up to 11 years on a parcel whose tax went unpaid, so a title search at closing will turn it up.

After April 15 the clerk holds the bill as a certificate of delinquency, interest builds by 1 percent each month, and the county attorney sends written notice well before a sale. Kentucky puts the sale 90 to 135 days after the handover. The clerk runs the list of unpaid bills in The Edmonson News in August and holds the sale in September at 11:00 a.m. Buyers register a few days ahead and post 25 percent of the face value of the certificates they hope to win.

Paying the clerk in full before the sale date ends the matter, and money that shows up later is sent back. Some bills are pulled from the list under KRS 134.504. Call 270-597-2624 for a payoff figure ahead of listing.

As grantor, the seller owes transfer tax of one dollar per $1,000 of price, which is how the $0.50 per $500 rate works out. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Edmonson County has 12,749 residents in 2025, a gain of 5.1 percent on the 2020 count. It covers 303 square miles of land inside the Bowling Green metro area, and Brownsville is the seat and only town. About a quarter of the county falls inside Mammoth Cave National Park, and the Green and Nolin rivers shape the rest.

Owners occupy 80.1 percent of housing, across 5,099 households. A typical owned home is worth $160,300 and a typical monthly rent runs $778. Because most owners hold their houses long term, sales tend to be of older homes. A seller facing back taxes or repairs can compare a listing against a straight as-is sale for cash.

sections.h2: What to do before you list
sections.html:
Start with the numbers. Call the sheriff at 270-597-2157 for this year's balance and the clerk at 270-597-2624 for any delinquent year. Look up the parcel on the PVA's qPublic search to see how the house is assessed, and phone 270-597-2381 if the acreage or building details look wrong. If you are 65 or disabled, check that the exemption is on the record, and keep copies of your payment receipts.

Then think about timing. A sale that closes in the middle of the collection year means the bill is split between you and the buyer, while a sale after February 1 means the 21 percent charge may already apply. An as-is cash sale can close quickly and pay the tax from your proceeds, which suits an inherited house or one that needs work.

faqs.q: When does the Edmonson County tax discount end?
faqs.a: The 2 percent discount ends on November 30 under the sheriff's calendar, because bills are mailed October 30. December is face value, and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Where does an Edmonson County owner send the payment?
faqs.a: Take it to the sheriff's office at 110 Jackson Street in Brownsville, or post a check or money order to that same address. The counter takes cash. Cards go through by phone or in the office and carry a fee.

faqs.q: Who sets my Edmonson County property value?
faqs.a: The PVA sets it, working from January 1 values. Its office is in the courthouse, phone 270-597-2381, and neither the sheriff nor the fiscal court has a say in the value.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Edmonson County assessment later in the year?
faqs.a: No. Every appeal starts with a PVA conference while the May tax roll is open to inspection, and the clerk's filing window closes one workday after the roll does.

faqs.q: What does Edmonson County do with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Bills left unpaid at the April 15 cutoff pass to the clerk, where 1 percent interest accrues monthly. The clerk advertises them in late summer and holds a tax sale, and payments must reach the clerk in full before the sale date.
